methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $47M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pivotal is a Growth-stage transportation company founded by Marcus Leng. The sector comprises three known private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride) and no public comparables, limiting conventional peer-median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised of $47M as a base value proxy, a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement yields $56M. This reflects the incremental value creation expected between funding rounds absent broader peer anchoring. Peer-median methodology was not applied due to insufficient comparable data: while three Transportation peers exist, none satisfy same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters simultaneously. A sector-wide median would introduce uncontrolled variance and is therefore excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $64M, centered at $56M. The low bound represents a conservative read of the $47M raised proxy; the high bound extrapolates to modest further step-up. Key uncertainties include Pivotal's capital efficiency relative to named peers, unit economics, and path to next funding event. The single-method reliance introduces material range width. Additional data on burn rate, revenue traction, or updated peer metrics would narrow this band materially.
